chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I never entered [the state of Ihram for Hajj] except as a Mutamatti', except in this year, for by Allah, I do not finish the Sa'i (circumambulation of the Kaaba) until my teeth chatter, and what you have done is better.' As for what has come regarding the virtue of Al-Mut'ah in Hajj, it is more than can be counted, among which is what he narrated:

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: The Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.تَتَقَلْقَلَ أَضْرَاسِي: My teeth chatter (indicating intense exertion or cold)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu', combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of performing Hajj as Mutamatti' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the superiority of Hajj al-Mut'ah by contrasting his usual practice with a specific year of intense devotion during Sa'i, where physical exertion was so great his teeth chattered. This narration serves as a foundational evidence for the Shia preference of combining Umrah and Hajj, emphasizing that the companions' adherence to this form was considered 'better' than other modes. The text introduces a vast corpus of hadiths reinforcing the virtue of Al-Mut'ah, underscoring its status as the most complete and rewarded form of pilgrimage in Shia jurisprudence.
